summary_paragraph: Mr. ___ was admitted with fever, cough, and hemoptysis in the setting of relapsed multiple myeloma and ongoing chemotherapy with Ninlaro and Revlimid. Initial evaluation revealed no pneumonia on chest X-ray or CT, but imaging showed bronchial wall thickening consistent with acute bronchitis. Sputum cultures were repeatedly contaminated and inconclusive. He had acute kidney injury likely exacerbated by infection and dehydration, which improved with IV fluids. His pancytopenia, a known complication of chemotherapy, was monitored without transfusion. Fever resolved with antibiotic therapy, and he improved clinically. He was discharged home in stable condition with instructions to complete antibiotics and follow up with oncology for further management of his myeloma and treatment planning.
